title: Which Version Should I Send?
prerequisites: Recognise filenames, version numbers, and calendar dates.
observable_outcome: The learner asks which document version to send, then confirms the exact filename and date in one checking question.
learning_objective: Clarify which document version to send, then confirm the filename and date accurately.

scenario.setting: A shared work folder before an email deadline.
scenario.prompt: A colleague writes: Please send the final proposal. The folder contains proposal_client_v3_12-Sep.pdf and proposal_client_v4_18-Sep.pdf. The word final does not identify one file.
scenario.puzzle: Which detail must you clarify before sending anything, and how can you check the complete filename?
scenario.privacy_note: The colleague, project, filenames, and dates are fictional teaching data.

model.clarify: Which version should I send, please?
model.confirm: So I should send proposal_client_v4_18-Sep.pdf, dated 18 September. Is that right?
model.neutral_variant: Do you mean version 4, dated 18 September?

language_focus.grammar: In the direct wh-question, use which version + should + subject + base verb: Which version should I send? In the checking question, Do you mean ...? is followed by the detail you want to verify.
language_focus.meaning: Version identifies a particular form of a document. The filename is the computer file's name. The date provides a second clue, so the readback checks both details before sending.
language_focus.appropriateness: Which version should I send, please? is clear and polite at work. Do you mean version 4, dated 18 September? is useful when you already have a likely choice but want confirmation. Avoid guessing from the word final when two files remain possible.
language_focus.detail_language: Latest means newest or most recent. A document dated 18 September has that date written on it. Say dated 18 September, without on.

choice_activity.prompt: The request says final, but two files are present. What must you clarify?

options.feedback: Correct. Final does not identify one of the two filenames, so ask which version.
The sender needs the correct file. The writer's identity does not distinguish these two versions.
The email route is already clear. The unresolved detail is the document version.

options.text: Which version should I send, please?
options.feedback: Correct. Which asks the colleague to choose from the known versions; should I send follows normal question order.

options.text: Do you mean version 4, dated 18 September?
options.feedback: Also correct when version 4 is your likely interpretation and you want a yes-or-no check.
This is not standard direct-question order. Ask Which version should I send?

slot_activity.prompt: Match each clue to its file-detail slot.

feedback.filename: Correct. This is the complete name of the computer file.
feedback.version: The filename contains a version marker, but the whole string is the filename.
feedback.date: The filename contains a date marker, but the whole string is not just a date.

feedback.filename: Version 4 identifies a form of the document, not the complete filename.
feedback.version: Correct. Version 4 selects the later numbered form.
feedback.date: Version 4 is a version label, not a calendar date.

feedback.filename: 18 September is not the complete filename.
feedback.version: The date supports the choice, but it is not the version number.
feedback.date: Correct. 18 September is the document date.

production_task.scenario: A manager asks for the latest budget report. You see budget_report_v2_03-Oct.xlsx and budget_report_v3_09-Oct.xlsx. The manager replies: version 3, dated 9 October.
production_task.instruction: Write one clarification question. Then write one complete confirmation with the filename and date.
acceptable_responses: Which version should I send, please? So I should send budget_report_v3_09-Oct.xlsx, dated 9 October. Is that right?
Do you mean version 3, dated 9 October? Let me check: budget_report_v3_09-Oct.xlsx. Is that correct?
rubric: I asked which version to send.
I repeated the date and invited confirmation.
production_task.valid_variants: Which version should I send? and Do you mean ...? can both work. File, document, proposal, and report are acceptable when they fit the situation.

review_prompt: Tomorrow, explain the word order in Which version should I send? Then give one checking question with Do you mean ...?

visual.title: Separate the clues, then confirm one file
visual.alt_text: A layered papercut flow. Two possible document files lead to a which-version question. The reply selects version 4 and 18 September. The exact filename and date then combine in one confirmation.
visual.prose: First notice that final does not identify one file. Ask which version to send. Use the reply to select the version number, filename, and date. Then repeat the complete filename and date and invite confirmation.

sources.title: Which

sources.title: Version
sources.inspected: Business English coverage defines a version as a document or product that differs from previous or later forms and lists current/latest/new version combinations.
sources.limitation: Used only to support the meaning of version. No dictionary examples are reproduced in the activity.

sources.title: Filename
sources.inspected: Filename is defined as the name given to a computer document or file.
sources.limitation: The filenames in this lesson are original fictional data.

sources.title: Date
sources.inspected: Business English coverage shows date as a verb meaning to put a day's date on something, including the pattern a letter dated 30 March.
sources.limitation: Used only to support the pattern dated plus date. The lesson uses original examples.
